رُبُوبِيَّةٌ [Lordship; or the state, or quality, of such as is termed رَبٌّ i. e. a lord, a possessor, an owner, or a proprietor; &c.: and, with the article ال particularly godship, godhead, or deity:] a subst. from الرَّبُّ; (T, * S, * M, K;) as also ↓ رِبَابَةٌ [which seems to be properly an inf. n. of 1 in the sense first explained]. (M, K.) ＝
-A2- Also, (M, K,) or ↓ رُبُوبَةٌ , (so in a copy of the K,) The state, or condition, of a مَمْلُوك [or slave]. (M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
